## What landed

- **`sig-ops release` verb family** (`ops/src/ops/release_pipeline.py` +
  `cli.py`) — `cut, build, stage, verify, classify, promote, rollback,
  clear-latest, withdraw, status`. Every verb takes `registry/LOCK`
  (create-if-absent precondition; a second writer refuses rather than
  queues; a stale lock clears only via `--break-lock <reason>` and the
  reason is journaled), refreshes a digest of the registry state files
  (`catalog.json`, `compat_index.json`, `withdrawals.json`,
  `latest.json`) and refuses on silent drift (stale-generation refusal),
  is resumable, and appends a `sig.release-event/1` record under
  `registry/events/`. `--dry-run` is the default; any write requires
  `--apply`. The verbs wrap the landed machinery
  (`release_candidate`/`release_publish_verify`/`release_serving`,
  `exports.release`, `release_identity` clock guards) — never
  re-implemented. `status` folds the event journal into the release
  state machine (`cut → built → staged → verified → promoted /
  superseded / rolled-back-from / withdrawn-whole / never-promoted`).
  Verbs whose behaviour later rows own are declared, locked, journaled
  and **refuse naming their owner** (RM-6 fail-closed): `promote` →
  P35.54, `rollback`/`clear-latest`/`withdraw` → P35.55, the V1–V14
  suite inside `verify` → P35.56/P35.58, `classify` → P35.60.
- **`ops/gcs.py`** — `GcsPreconditionFailed` + `insert_object(…,
  if_generation_match=0)` + `get_object_meta`; HTTP 412 is an explicit
  refusal signal, not a retry.
- **Private release bucket IaC** (`ops/gcp/release-infra.sh`,
  `release-bucket-lifecycle.json`, `config.sh`) — `gs://${SIG_GCP_PROJECT}
  -sig-release`: uniform bucket-level access, public-access-prevention,
  versioning, 30-day noncurrent lifecycle; the §4.1 namespace
  `staged/{r,v,s,releases}/<pub>/` + `registry/{catalog.json,
  compat_index.json, withdrawals.json, activations/, events/, LOCK,
  conf/<gen>/}` + `status/**`; IAM: `sig-release-rt` writes all but
  `status/**`, `sig-status-rt` writes `status/**` only, restricted export
  readers — **no `allUsers`/`allAuthenticatedUsers`** anywhere.
- **IAM-only staging origins** — `sig-web-staging` / `sig-api-staging`
  Cloud Run services on the same image digests production runs,
  `--no-allow-unauthenticated`, `SIG_STAGING=1`, scale-to-zero; identity
  token only.
- **`sig-release` job + `sig-release-rt`** — the ACT-13 least-privilege
  pattern; the job runs as the reserved service account, never the
  default Editor SA; its entrypoint refuses bare execution.
- **NEW-5 eviction** — the nine committed release-tree/registry subtrees
  under `docs/build/reports/` (1,616 files: `candidate_release`,
  `corpus_release`, `corpus_registry`, `staging_registry`, `rehearsal`,
  `release`, `registry`) are deleted — files, not history (G3 RM-8);
  the per-root inventory lives in
  `docs/build/reports/EVICTION_NEW-5_P35.53.md` and
  `scripts/ci/release_tree_guard.py` refuses recommit (publication-shaped
  directories, staged/release namespaces, registry files and `LOCK`).
- **Fixture conversion** — `tests/ops/candidate_fixture.py` rebuilds the
  candidate packet at runtime from the still-committed recovery/export
  inputs via the real `exports.release` machinery (DB-dependent portions
  honestly labelled `synthesized_fixture`); `test_journey_verify.py` and
  `test_release_publish_verify.py` consume it, and `journey_verify`
  reports an absent candidate tree through checks instead of crashing.
- **`memory_guard.py` deletion attribution** — a whole-file deletion of
  a protected record attributed to no commit in range mode
  (`commit_of_removed(path, "")` could only match a removed *line*), so
  the `seed-commit` exemption could never cover a mandated eviction. The
  attribution pass now records the deleting commit per `+++ /dev/null`
  diff; findings still fire unless the deleter is declared — declared:
  `seed-commit 6059a98b` in `history.policy`.
